messages.subject: Sampling from a lookup table
parts:
We have estimated posterior distributions of measurement errors for each observation in our data set.

The posterior distributions are relatively smooth.

When fitting our observations to a model, is there a way in Stan to sample from a lookup table containing these posteriors, in order to marginalize over measurement errors ?

Thanks!

messages.author: 3f24cff75a03e8f0
messages.subject: Re: Sampling from a lookup table
parts:
Hi Joseph,

So it ain't pretty, but here's what we had to do. First, you need to build a function that typecasts floats to ints, since doing so is not native to the Stan language. This function does so quickly, by binary search:

    int as_integer_bsearch(real i_this, int size_max) {
        // Outputs int(floor(i_this)), assuming that i_this is non-negative
        int right_bound;
        int left_bound;
        int mid;
        
        right_bound <- size_max;
        left_bound  <- 0;
        mid <- (right_bound + left_bound)/ 2; // int division intentional
        
        // special case
        if(i_this == right_bound) {
            return right_bound;
        }
        if(i_this == left_bound) {
            return left_bound;
        }
        
        while(mid != left_bound && mid != right_bound) {
            if( i_this < mid ) {
                right_bound <- mid;
            }
            else {
                left_bound <- mid;
            }
            mid <- (right_bound + left_bound)/ 2;
        }
        return mid;
    }


Then here is the function that does the interpolation. The lookup_tbl has to be provided as data. For our particular problem, we had one regime where linear interpolation made the most sense, and another for logarithmic. Note that we are also coding in the left and right tail behaviors for the function (log-pdf of the Landau distribution):


    real landau_logp(real[] lookup_tbl, 
                                int nrow_lkup_tbl, 
                                real x_lo, 
                                real x_hi, 
                                real x_linstep,
                                real x_breakpt,
                                int idx_breakpt,
                                real x_log10step,
                                real x_this) {
        // Outputs Landau logpdf, using linear interpolation (to left of breakpoint), log interpolation
        // (to right of breakpoint), or tail behavior.
        // lookup_tbl: Provided as data
        // nrow_lkup_tbl: # rows in lookup_tbl
        // x_lo, x_hi: Outside these bounds, use analytic formulas for tail behavior
        // x_breakpt: Below this value, lookup table is given in linear steps; above it is logarithmic
        // idx_breakpt: Index of the breakpoint in the table
        // x_linstep: Linear step size
        // x_log10step: Log10 step size
        // x_this: The value to compute
        
        real log10_x_this;
        real x_a; // x-value to left of x_this in table
        int idx_a; // index of x_a in table
        real f_a; // log-prob of x_a
        real f_b; // log-prob of x_b (value to right of x_this in table)
        real perc; // Used in interpolation
        
        if( x_this < -365) {
            return negative_infinity(); // at -365, log-prob is -5e306
        }
        if( x_this < x_lo ) {
            return -exp( pow(-x_this,1.20591) / 1.741504 ); // left tail behavior, determined numerically
        }
        if (x_this > x_hi) {
            return  -2 * log(x_this); // right tail behavior
        }
        
        if(x_this > x_breakpt) {
            // Logarithmic interpolation (i.e., linear interpolation on log(x))
            log10_x_this <- log10(x_this);
            idx_a <- idx_breakpt + as_integer_bsearch((log10_x_this - log10(x_breakpt))/x_log10step, nrow_lkup_tbl);
            x_a <- x_breakpt * pow(10, x_log10step * (idx_a - idx_breakpt));
            perc <- (log10_x_this - log10(x_a)) / x_log10step;
        } else {
            // Linear interpolation
            idx_a <- 1 + as_integer_bsearch( (x_this - x_lo)/x_linstep, nrow_lkup_tbl);
            x_a   <- x_lo + x_linstep * (idx_a - 1);
            perc <- (x_this - x_a)/x_linstep;
        }
        
        f_a <- lookup_tbl[idx_a];
        f_b <- lookup_tbl[idx_a+1];
        
        return f_a  + (f_b - f_a) * perc;
    }


Hope this helps!

Best,
Daniel

parts:
If you define your functions with suffix _lpdf (real outcome)
or _lpmf (discrete outcome), then you can use sampling notation.
See the manual chapter on user-defined functions for details
and examples.

The reason we don't have the real to int conversion built in is
that it breaks derivatives so you have to be very careful
that the result of whatever you do is still continuously
differentiable or Stan's HMC will have a hard time
sampling through the discontinuity.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Sampling from a lookup table
parts:
The reason we don't have the real to int conversion built in is
that it breaks derivatives so you have to be very careful
that the result of whatever you do is still continuously
differentiable or Stan's HMC will have a hard time
sampling through the discontinuity.

In particular, the discontinuities at the interpolation points
will prevent the discrete trajectories used in HMC from
following the true trajectories that are needed for scalable
sampling.  The acceptance probability will suffer from this
inaccuracy and you will not really be taking advantage of
the potential performance of Stan.

Aside from a few (important) exceptions, interpolation
is evil.  Evil evil evil.

        // lookup_tbl: Provided as data

        // x_lo, x_hi: Outside these bounds, use analytic formulas for tail behavior
        // x_linstep: Linear step size
        // x_this: The value to compute

        int idx_a; // index of x_a in table
        real f_a; // log-prob of x_a
        real f_b; // log-prob of x_b (value to right of x_this in table)
        real perc; // Used in interpolation
        
        if( x_this < -365) {
            return negative_infinity(); // at -365, log-prob is -5e306
        }
        if( x_this < x_lo ) {
            return negative_infinity(); // left tail behavior
        }
        if (x_this > x_hi) {
            return  negative_infinity(); // right tail behavior
        }
        
        // Linear interpolation
        idx_a <- 1 + as_integer_bsearch( (x_this - x_lo)/x_linstep, nrow_lkup_tbl);
        x_a   <- x_lo + x_linstep * (idx_a - 1);
        perc <- (x_this - x_a)/x_linstep;
        
        
        f_a <- lookup_tbl[idx_a];
        f_b <- lookup_tbl[idx_a+1];
        
        return f_a  + (f_b - f_a) * perc;
    }

> >         int left_bound;

> >             return right_bound;
> >         }

> >             return left_bound;
> >         }

> >             }

> >             }

> >         }
> >         return mid;
> >     }

parts:
Hi Daniel

Is size_max the length of the lookup table, or is it the zero-based index of the last element of the lookup table?

I.e. if the lookup table had 20 elements, would size_max be 20 or 19?

Joe
On 09/13/2016 07:16 PM, Daniel Rosenbloom wrote:

Hi Joseph,

So it ain't pretty, but here's what we had to do. First, you need to build a function that typecasts floats to ints, since doing so is not native to the Stan language. This function does so quickly, by binary search:

    int as_integer_bsearch(real i_this, int size_max) {
        // Outputs int(floor(i_this)), assuming that i_this is non-negative
        int right_bound;
        int left_bound;
        int mid;
        
        right_bound <- size_max;
        left_bound  <- 0;
        mid <- (right_bound + left_bound)/ 2; // int division intentional
        
        // special case
        if(i_this == right_bound) {
            return right_bound;
        }
        if(i_this == left_bound) {
            return left_bound;
        }
        
        while(mid != left_bound && mid != right_bound) {
            if( i_this < mid ) {
                right_bound <- mid;
            }
            else {
                left_bound <- mid;
            }
            mid <- (right_bound + left_bound)/ 2;
        }
        return mid;
    }


Then here is the function that does the interpolation. The lookup_tbl has to be provided as data. For our particular problem, we had one regime where linear interpolation made the most sense, and another for logarithmic. Note that we are also coding in the left and right tail behaviors for the function (log-pdf of the Landau distribution):


    real landau_logp(real[] lookup_tbl, 
                                int nrow_lkup_tbl, 
                                real x_lo, 
                                real x_hi, 
                                real x_linstep,
                                real x_breakpt,
                                int idx_breakpt,
                                real x_log10step,
                                real x_this) {
        // Outputs Landau logpdf, using linear interpolation (to left of breakpoint), log interpolation
        // (to right of breakpoint), or tail behavior.
        // lookup_tbl: Provided as data
        // nrow_lkup_tbl: # rows in lookup_tbl
        // x_lo, x_hi: Outside these bounds, use analytic formulas for tail behavior
        // x_breakpt: Below this value, lookup table is given in linear steps; above it is logarithmic
        // idx_breakpt: Index of the breakpoint in the table
        // x_linstep: Linear step size
        // x_log10step: Log10 step size
        // x_this: The value to compute
        
        real log10_x_this;
        real x_a; // x-value to left of x_this in table
        int idx_a; // index of x_a in table
        real f_a; // log-prob of x_a
        real f_b; // log-prob of x_b (value to right of x_this in table)
        real perc; // Used in interpolation
        
        if( x_this < -365) {
            return negative_infinity(); // at -365, log-prob is -5e306
        }
        if( x_this < x_lo ) {
            return -exp( pow(-x_this,1.20591) / 1.741504 ); // left tail behavior, determined numerically
        }
        if (x_this > x_hi) {
            return  -2 * log(x_this); // right tail behavior
        }
        
        if(x_this > x_breakpt) {
            // Logarithmic interpolation (i.e., linear interpolation on log(x))
            log10_x_this <- log10(x_this);
            idx_a <- idx_breakpt + as_integer_bsearch((log10_x_this - log10(x_breakpt))/x_log10step, nrow_lkup_tbl);
            x_a <- x_breakpt * pow(10, x_log10step * (idx_a - idx_breakpt));
            perc <- (log10_x_this - log10(x_a)) / x_log10step;
        } else {
            // Linear interpolation
            idx_a <- 1 + as_integer_bsearch( (x_this - x_lo)/x_linstep, nrow_lkup_tbl);
            x_a   <- x_lo + x_linstep * (idx_a - 1);
            perc <- (x_this - x_a)/x_linstep;
        }
        
        f_a <- lookup_tbl[idx_a];
        f_b <- lookup_tbl[idx_a+1];
        
        return f_a  + (f_b - f_a) * perc;
    }


Hope this helps!

Best,
Daniel
